acceptanceClaims: the original controller was SIGKILLed at the accepted root-veth partial state and a first successor acquired recovery authority against the inherited durable ledger digest
the first successor moved q into the peer-B namespace, moved w into the fabric namespace, attached w to the bridge, and was SIGKILLed before link-up/address/service/stable topology publication
the durable ledger digest before the first successor mutation and after its physical progress was exactly identical, proving durable ledger generation is not a physical-world progress version
a second successor acquired recovery authority against that same durable digest, preserved the first successor as predecessor claim lineage, and independently re-observed the changed Host midpoint
the second successor executed only the missing suffix, did not replay the whole effect, and then published a new stable peer-b-present durable generation
the same Windows Guest completed peer A and peer B across the original controller death plus the first successor death, while one surviving packet capture observed both flows
after the second successor was SIGKILLed, final reconciliation preserved current plus archived recovery lineage and closed the world with zero residuals
limitations: only the exact after-veth-placement-and-bridge-before-link-up successor fault point was physically accepted
the experiment does not prove recovery from non-persistent or externally ambiguous effect progress
the second successor was not itself interrupted during the missing suffix
the acceptance receipt preserves the midpoint observation, but production successor claim metadata does not claim to retain a full physical handoff snapshot
the experiment is single-host and does not prove distributed fencing or partition recovery
generic exactly-once semantics, shared-resource concurrency and causal-DAG requirements remain unproved
the accepted Range remains structurally unrouted and does not authorize external or uncontrolled targets
